Unmodified publisher JPEG; shader provides a restrained display-only night emission and daylight fade.

encoding: lossless WebP; achromatic RGB decode of one grayscale coverage channel

validation.comparison: Complete decode equals soft-toe-before-BOX coverage, not original display-image codes

acquisition_epoch: 2001 multiday composite, released 2002; not simulated epoch or live weather
transform: Verify each original NASA grayscale hemisphere, apply the documented 256-code pointwise display-only soft-toe LUT to native texels, then BOX-reduce each hemisphere to4096square and join W then E into8192x4096. BOX-reduce that result2x2 to4096x2048. Encode lossless WebP. No geographic painting, synthetic clouds, sharpening or gap filling. The remap precedes all spatial reduction; runtime does not apply a second transfer to these global coverage values.
source_limitation: The checked western and eastern source images have a hard cloud-coverage discontinuity at longitude 0 degrees, visible over the Southern Ocean. This fixed geographical seam is preserved in both the global maps and native tiles; it is not a runtime tile boundary.

display_transfer.purpose: Display-only low-code suppression of visible NASA composite swath plateaus; not a calibrated cloud fraction, optical depth or gamma correction.
display_transfer.formula: For source code c in[0,255], t=min(1,c/64); output=floor(c*t*t*(3-2*t)+0.5). Codes64..255 are unchanged.
display_transfer.quantization: 8-bit R8/gray coverage, round-half-up in both Python and JavaScript. Codes0..9 map to0; genuine faint cloud signal is reduced along with source artifacts.
display_transfer.filter_order: Apply to native source/decoded tile texels before area reduction or GPU mip generation. Never apply the nonlinear toe to an already filtered coverage sample.
